findings.title: Case-sensitive lookup allows blocked addresses to register
findings.body: BlockedEmail looks up the supplied email with an exact, case-sensitive equality comparison, and neither this model nor User.new_from_params normalizes it. A block for `block@example.com` therefore does not stop registration with `block@EXAMPLE.COM`, even though the domain refers to the same mailbox. Normalize addresses consistently when storing blocked entries and checking user emails so casing cannot bypass the block.

findings.title: Concurrent matches lose counter increments
findings.body: The match counter is updated using a read-modify-save sequence without locking. Two simultaneous checks for the same blocked email can both read the same match_count and save the same incremented value, recording only one match instead of two. Use an atomic database increment or a locked update to preserve the statistics under concurrent registration attempts.
